privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: The only thing this casino never gambles with is your data. vibe-gambling knows nothing about your work. This page says exactly what this instance stores, why, where, for how long and how to delete it.
privacy.instance.unknown: The details of this instance (who runs it, where it is hosted, how to contact them) could not be loaded. Reload the page to try again.
privacy.sent.title: What leaves your computer
privacy.sent.body: Per turn, the Claude Code plugin sends only: a random turn id, the turn duration, two yes/no flags (a successful git push happened, a test command failed), the plugin version, the generic OS (linux, darwin, win32 or other) and your session token. Never prompts, answers, code, commands, file names, paths or repositories. The two flags are computed on your computer from the Bash commands, which are then forgotten.
privacy.sent.commands: When you use a command, what you type in it is sent too: the amount and square of /bet, your login when confirming /vibe-delete-account.
privacy.stored.title: What the server stores
privacy.stored.body: From your GitHub profile: numeric id, login, avatar URL and the date the account was created. Your settings: hidden from the leaderboard or not, language. The game: your wallet per season, rounds and turns (when each one started and ended, result, bets, turn duration and the two flags), loans, streaks, unlocked achievements and the Hall of Ruin. Sessions: the hash of each token (never the token itself), its kind (plugin or window) and when it was used and expires.
privacy.stored.not: Not stored: the GitHub token (thrown away right after reading your public profile; login asks for no permissions), the plugin version or the OS (checked and dropped), your IP address (only held in memory for rate limiting, never written down), whether the window is in view (only in memory while it is connected, to decide if a prompt spins live or is saved as a pending spin), and no URLs, headers or tokens in the logs.
privacy.why.title: Why
privacy.why.body: To run the game: keep your fake balance, resolve spins and show the public leaderboard. Nothing else. No ads, no analytics, no tracking cookies, no data sold or shared.
privacy.why.basis: Legal basis (GDPR, art. 6): providing the service you ask for when you log in (6.1.b), and a legitimate interest in keeping it secure: rate limits, backups and logs without personal data (6.1.f).
privacy.where.title: Where
privacy.where.instance: This instance is run by {operator} and hosted on {hosting}.
privacy.where.proxy: {proxy} sits in front of it as a network proxy: it sees your IP address and the requests passing through, like any CDN, and gets nothing else from the server.
privacy.where.images: Your browser loads the GitHub avatars of the leaderboard straight from {origins}, which therefore sees your IP address.
privacy.where.noImages: This instance loads no images from other sites.
privacy.where.github: You log in through GitHub, under its own privacy policy. There are no other third parties.
privacy.howLong.title: For how long
privacy.howLong.body: Your account, games and Hall of Ruin entries: until you delete your account. Leaderboard rows of closed seasons stay in the Hall of Ruin unless you hide yourself or delete your account.
privacy.howLong.sessions: Sessions: {mod} for the plugin and {web} for the window, from login or until you log out; then they are deleted. An unfinished GitHub login: until it finishes or expires.
privacy.howLong.link: The link that opens the window: {link}, single use; then it is deleted.
privacy.howLong.ip: Your IP address: {ip} in memory for rate limiting, counted from your first request; then it is forgotten.
privacy.howLong.backups: Backups are kept for {backups}, so a deleted account may remain in them until then.
privacy.cookies.title: Cookies
privacy.cookies.body: One session cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict) so this window knows who you are, until it expires or you log out. Settings like sound, the CRT filter or the language stay in your own browser and never leave it. No tracking cookies.
privacy.leaderboard.title: Public leaderboard
privacy.leaderboard.body: By default your login, avatar and stats appear in the public leaderboard; you are told so when you log in. Hide them any time with /vibe-hide or in the window settings (you also leave the Hall of Ruin, past seasons included); /vibe-show brings you back.
privacy.leaderboard.newAccounts: GitHub accounts younger than {days} days play as usual but only appear in the leaderboard and the Hall of Ruin once they turn {days} days old, so that mass-created accounts are not worth it. That is the only use of your GitHub account's creation date, which is refreshed at every login and deleted with your account.
privacy.delete.title: Delete your account
privacy.delete.body: Run /vibe-delete-account in Claude Code and confirm with your login. Every row about you is deleted at once, Hall of Ruin included, and your windows are closed.
privacy.delete.rights: /balance and the window show what there is about you; ask (see Contact) for a full copy. Your login and avatar are refreshed from GitHub every time you log in. If you think something was not handled properly, you can complain to your data protection authority.
privacy.contact.title: Contact
privacy.contact.body: {operator} is responsible for the data on this instance. Write to {contact}; please keep personal data out of public places and ask for a private channel if you need one.
privacy.referral.title: Affiliate program
privacy.referral.body: If you ask for your affiliate link (/vibe-invite or the AFFILIATES screen), a random code is created for you; it says nothing about you. If you redeem someone’s code, the server stores who invited whom, when, the welcome bonus and, once you activate, the commission paid to them. It is used only to run the program and its anti-abuse rules (one code per account, no cycles, a cap per season). The invite page /r/<code> shows the login and avatar of whoever shares it, unless they are hidden from the leaderboard. Whoever invited you only sees numbers (how many are invited and activated), never who you are. When you delete your account, your side of every invite is erased: what remains has nobody attached and only keeps counting towards the other person’s seasonal cap; if neither side is left, the row is deleted.
